problem: Raw paper/source count and flat lineage labels can overstate corroboration when apparently distinct evidence descends from shared datasets, analyses, intellectual ancestors, or alternate identifiers.
registered_claim_boundary: A provenance graph can establish known shared ancestry or absence of known shared ancestry under the registered graph. It cannot by itself establish statistical, causal, or epistemic independence.

worlds.description: Two evidence items have different IDs but the same direct parent source.
Two analyses descend through different intermediate nodes from one remote dataset root.
Two evidence items have complete, disjoint registered provenance roots.
At least one selected evidence item has explicitly incomplete ancestry.
A selected evidence item references a parent absent from the registered graph.
The registered derivation graph contains a cycle reachable from selected evidence.
Two evidence IDs are declared alternates of the same underlying evidence entity.
Two evidence items are specializations/versions of one common source entity.
Two selected items share one registered root even though each also has a unique root.
Three selected items form one two-item shared-ancestry component plus one disjoint item.
Graph contains duplicate node identifiers with conflicting definitions.
No evidence items are selected for corroboration assessment.
A selected evidence identifier is absent from the graph.
Permuting node and selected-item order must not change the report.
Disjoint registered roots must not be labeled statistically or epistemically independent.
A generator family that passes flat lineage-ID checks is downgraded when graph ancestry reveals a common root.
Generator corroboration cannot claim independent support when selected evidence ancestry is incomplete.
Generator proposal may retain proposal status when registered evidence roots are complete and disjoint, but still gains no target authority.
Any lineage report or generator-lineage report must not activate canonical scientific knowledge or grant target authority.
Graph topology alone must not invent a statistical effective sample size or independence probability.

falsifier: If lineage-aware graph support fails to detect frozen shared-ancestry worlds or adds no discrimination beyond flat labels on duplicated-ancestry tests, retain provenance records only and do not add corroboration logic.
real_utility_boundary: Synthetic support validation does not establish improved real scientific evidence synthesis; a future frozen real duplicated-ancestry corpus is required for empirical utility.
